newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore cuts tax rate for fund management.
newsitem.headline: Singapore cuts tax rate for fund management.

text.p: Singapore will cut the tax rate for fund managers managing more than Singapore $5 billion of non-resident funds to five percent on incremental income earned with effect from the 1996 year of assessment, Finance Minister Richard Hu said on Friday.
Fund managers previously enjoyed a concessionary 10 percent tax rate on income earned from managing non-resident funds, Hu said in his budget speech.

He added fund managers with substantial operations in Singapore would be exempted from tax on income earned from non-resident funds to encourage them to further expand their business in Singapore and to use the city-state as a regional base.

To qualify for a tax exemption, fund managers would need to be managing at least S$10 billion of non-resident funds, employ at least seven professionals and analysts and have been operating for three years under Singapore's tax exemption for fund managers scheme.
Hu said the incentive would be granted for an initial period of five years with effect from the 1998 year of assessment.
He said there were 161 fund managers operating in Singapore managing funds totalling more than S$125 billion.
Hu also announced tax incentives for Asian Currency Unit (ACU) activities.
Banks and merchant banks are currently taxed at a concessionary rate of 10 percent on income earned from ACU activities.

There was also a further reduction in the tax rate to five percent on the incremental income derived from certain high value activities, provided the taxable income of some of these activities exceeds S$10 million, Hu said.
He said the five percent tax on incremental income would be extended to income derived from all taxable ACU activities, provided this figure exceeded S$50 million.
He said this new incentive would be granted for an initial five year period with effect from the 1998 year of assessment.
